modules.title: Python Basics for AI Engineers
modules.why: Every later module is written in Python. A week spent making the basics automatic pays for itself many times over - and every exercise here uses invoice data, so you're already thinking like AuditGate.
objectives: Run Python interactively and run a file from the terminal
Work with strings, numbers, lists and dictionaries
Write functions with if-statements and for-loops
Handle 'nothing' safely with None
Spot and fix the shared-default-list bug

code_along.title: Meet the interactive shell
code_along.task: Run `uv run python`, then try: 2 + 2, name = 'Acme', name.upper(), [1, 2, 3][0], {'total': 40}['total']. Type exit() to leave.

code_along.title: Read the official tutorial
code_along.task: Read sections 3 (An Informal Introduction), 4.1-4.8 (Control Flow) and 5.1-5.5 (Data Structures). Type every example yourself rather than copy-pasting.

code_along.title: Exercises 1-4: strings, numbers, loops
code_along.task: Replace each `raise NotImplementedError(...)` with your code. Run the checkpoint after each one and watch tests turn green.

code_along.title: Exercises 5-9: dictionaries, conditions, None
code_along.task: These are the patterns AuditGate's code uses everywhere: counting, grouping, filtering, and handling empty input.

code_along.title: Exercise 10: fix the privacy bug
code_along.task: collect_tokens() leaks data between calls (assessment question PY2). Fix it, then explain to yourself in one sentence why it happened.

code_along.title: Compare with the reference
code_along.task: Only after your tests pass: compare your answers with the solutions and read the 'Shorter' comments - that's the next step in fluency.

modules.milestone: You can read and write the Python that AuditGate is built from.
modules.stretch: Rewrite exercises 4, 7 and 9 as one-liners using sum(), a list comprehension and max(key=...).

modules.title: Typed Data & Validation Schemas
modules.why: Every reliable AI system starts with a precise definition of 'correct output'. If you can't describe an invoice in types, no model can fill it in reliably.
objectives: Use dicts, lists, sets, dataclasses and comprehensions fluently on document data
Model real business documents as Pydantic v2 schemas with Decimal money and ISO dates
Separate field validation (what's on the page) from audit rules (does it add up)
Read and act on a ValidationError

code_along.title: Read the schemas
code_along.task: Read Invoice, Bid and WorkOrder. Explain to yourself why audit() is a method and not a validator.

code_along.title: Break it on purpose
code_along.task: uv run python -c "from auditgate.extraction.schemas import Invoice; Invoice(vendor_name='', invoice_number='1', total='abc')" - read every line of the ValidationError.

code_along.title: Add a rule
code_along.task: Add an Invoice audit rule DUPLICATE_LINE that warns when two line items share a description and amount. Add a test for it.

code_along.title: Add a field
code_along.task: Add an optional `po_number: str | None` to Invoice and teach HeuristicExtractor to read 'PO #:' lines.

modules.milestone: AuditGate can represent and audit invoices, bids and work orders without any AI at all.
modules.stretch: Add a fourth document type: Receipt (merchant, date, payment method last-4, total).

modules.title: LLM API Mechanics & Structured Outputs
modules.why: Clients pay for answers they can trust. Structured outputs turn a chatty model into a function that returns a validated object - or fails loudly.
objectives: Call OpenAI, Anthropic and a local Ollama model through one interface
Use instructor to get Pydantic objects back, with validation-driven retries
Handle rate limits, timeouts and token budgets
Write prompts that resist prompt injection inside documents

code_along.title: Run a local model
code_along.task: Install Ollama, `ollama pull llama3.1`, set AUDITGATE_PROVIDER=local, then run `uv run python -m auditgate.evals.runner --provider local`.

code_along.title: Trace a request
code_along.task: Read LLMExtractor.extract. Identify the system prompt rule that defends against inv_prompt_injection.

code_along.title: Compare providers
code_along.task: Run the eval for heuristic and one LLM provider with --report. Diff the two JSON reports and write down where each wins.

code_along.title: Add timing
code_along.task: Record extraction latency in AuditReport (a new `latency_ms` field) and show it in the UI.

modules.milestone: AuditGate can swap between offline, local-LLM and hosted-LLM extraction with one setting.
modules.stretch: Add a 'consensus' extractor that runs two backends and flags fields where they disagree.

modules.title: Data Security & PII Sanitization
modules.why: This is the product's moat. Business owners don't fear AI - they fear their customers' bank details ending up in someone else's logs.
objectives: Detect PII and financial identifiers with validated regexes (Luhn, SSN rules)
Implement reversible tokenization: sanitize -> extract -> rehydrate
Combine deterministic detection with optional spaCy NER for recall
Measure leakage instead of hoping
concepts: threat model: what leaves the machine?

code_along.title: Read the sanitizer
code_along.task: Follow one value from Detector -> _spans -> _resolve_overlaps -> Vault.token_for -> rehydrate.

code_along.title: Enable NER
code_along.task: uv pip install en_core_web_sm (see README), then run the eval with --spacy and compare redaction counts.

code_along.title: Add a detector
code_along.task: Add DRIVERS_LICENSE detection anchored on labels like 'DL #:' and add a golden-dataset case with it in pii_values.

code_along.title: Attack it
code_along.task: Write a case designed to leak (e.g. a phone number written as 512 555 0147). Watch the eval fail, then fix the detector.

modules.milestone: No raw PII ever reaches an extraction backend, and the eval proves it on every run.
modules.stretch: Encrypt the Vault at rest with a per-session key so even local crash dumps are safe.

modules.title: Agent Workflows & Orchestration
modules.why: Real work is multi-step: load, clean, extract, verify, route to a human. Orchestration is where reliability is won or lost.
objectives: Design a pipeline as explicit, testable stages with a typed report
Route outcomes (pass / review / fail) to humans with reasons
Expose the engine over a local FastAPI service
Process batches concurrently with bounded parallelism

code_along.title: Read the pipeline
code_along.task: Map each line of process_text to a stage. Where would you add a second-opinion step?

code_along.title: Serve it
code_along.task: uv run uvicorn auditgate.api:app --port 8000, then POST a golden-dataset document to /audit/text.

code_along.title: Batch mode
code_along.task: Add process_folder(path, concurrency=4) that audits every file in a folder and writes a summary CSV with pandas.

code_along.title: Escalation agent
code_along.task: When status is FAIL, draft (don't send) a polite query email to the vendor explaining each finding.

modules.milestone: AuditGate runs as a local service that can audit a folder of documents and route exceptions.
modules.stretch: Re-implement the pipeline as a LangGraph graph (see tutorials/langgraph) with a human approval interrupt.

modules.title: Automated Evaluations & Shipping the MVP
modules.why: 'It worked on my demo' doesn't sell. A scored, repeatable eval is both your engineering safety net and your best sales asset.
objectives: Build and grow a golden dataset of real edge cases
Gate releases on accuracy, schema adherence and zero PII leakage
Ship a polished local Streamlit dashboard
Package the pitch: privacy and reliability in plain language

code_along.title: Run the gate
code_along.task: uv run python -m auditgate.evals.runner --report eval_report.json and read every metric.

code_along.title: Grow the dataset
code_along.task: Add 5 cases from (anonymised) real documents a prospect sends you. Keep the gate green.

code_along.title: Polish the UI
code_along.task: uv run streamlit run auditgate/ui.py - add a batch upload tab and an export-to-Excel button (openpyxl).

code_along.title: Sell it
code_along.task: Customise the pitch for one niche (e.g. property managers). Book three demos.

modules.milestone: A demo-ready, evaluated, local-first MVP and a pitch you can hand to a business owner.
modules.stretch: Add a GitHub Action that runs pytest + the eval runner on every push.
